twenty ninth sunday in ordinary time - year a- 18th october 2026 the question as to whether or not it was lawful to pay taxes to caesar was a very serious one, and it really put jesus in a spot. if he said it was lawful, he would be regarded as a traitor to the jewish cause and the jewish religion. if he said it was unlawful, he could be denounced as fomenting rebellion against rome. jesus replied: “give to caesar what belongs to caesar, and to god what belongs to god”(for caesar we can substitute the stte). this doesn’t mean that there are some things that belong to caesar and others that belong to god, as if reality were divisible into ‘secular’ and ‘sacred’. it means that an obligation to caesar stands under and is judged by a paramount obligation: to acknowledge the sovereignity of god. jesus was implying that there need not be conflict between the demands of the state and those of god. the state has a role, but its power is limited and does not supplant god. from this principle christians deduced that they could accommodate loyalty to the state. as christians we have dual citizenship. we are citizens of the country in which we happen to be living or in which we were born. to many benefits. to its forces of law and order we owe the fact that we are able to live in peace and security. to its public services we owe transport, water, light, etc. to its social provisions we have access to education, medical care, and so on. but as christians we are also citizens of the kingdom of god. to it we priviledges, and to it we also have obligations. in most cases the two responsibilities do not clash. but at times they may. and when they do, christians will spontaneously know which comes first. as christians our first and deepest loyalty is to god. to god alone we render worship. in order things we gladly acknowledge and serve the secular powers, praying that they will rule wisely and justly. culled from: new sunday and holy day liturgies, year a by flor mccarthy sdb

safeguarding sunday 22nd february 2026 training a special word of thanks to our diocesan safeguarding trainers, trish o’neill & ailish higgins who facilitated 10 training events in 2025. a total number of 177 church personnel, including clergy, religious, staff and volunteers trained in 2025. the diocesan safeguarding committee joined the ossory safeguarding committee and attended training facilitated by the national board in kilkenny 17th november 2025. the training focused on the role of safeguarding committees in the context of our national church policy and standards for safeguarding children. ballyadams
